channel.title: Tech Destination Sri Lanka
channel.description: Connecting the world to Sri Lanka's technology ecosystem

item.title: Sri Lankan engineers help build Norway's leading digital health platform. Meet Creative Software
item.description: A Colombo company founded in 1999 has spent 25 years as the engineering partner behind DIPS, Norway's largest health records provider.

item.title: A Colombo team built Sri Lanka's first AI gateway, with 200+ models billed in rupees. Meet Roar Global
item.description: Roar started as a digital publisher in 2014. It is now an AI led venture builder with 150+ specialists and no outside capital.

item.title: Six engineers with no funding and no office built an 80 person AI software company. Meet Xeynergy
item.description: Bootstrapped in 2021, Xeynergy now earns multi million dollar recurring revenue and ships its own AI products.

item.title: A publicly listed Swedish tech company calls its Colombo office its global tech center. Meet Frontwalker
item.description: Frontwalker Group has built enterprise and public sector software for 35+ years. Its 100+ engineers in Sri Lanka carry delivery for the whole group.

item.title: An ASX listed telecom challenger runs 24x7 network operations from Colombo. Meet Superloop
item.description: Superloop serves 400,000+ customers in Australia. Engineers in Sri Lanka help keep its national network running around the clock.

item.title: The private equity firms behind IFS bet on Sri Lanka again, this time inside Port City Colombo. Meet IGT1 Lanka
item.description: EQT, Hg and TA Associates launched a second, fully export oriented technology company in Sri Lanka in 2025.

item.title: The software that designs the world's microchips is partly engineered in Colombo. Meet Synopsys Sri Lanka
item.description: Synopsys opened its Sri Lanka R&D operation in 2015. The Colombo team works on core chip design and verification products.

item.title: One of the world's largest tyre makers runs IT support for Asia from Colombo. Meet Michelin's Sri Lanka hub
item.description: 100+ IT professionals at Orion City keep Michelin's business technology running across a continent.

item.title: A Norwegian software company has run its core engineering from Colombo for 15 years. Meet Tiqri
item.description: 150 developers, 250+ projects and client relationships that have lasted more than a decade.

item.title: A Colombo based team handles revenue operations for US healthcare, then bought an American company. Meet HealthRecon Connect
item.description: HITRUST certified and 1,500+ people strong, with Sri Lanka as its main operational base.

item.title: The barcode technology tracking your parcels is partly built in Colombo. Meet Zebra Technologies Lanka
item.description: The Nasdaq listed leader in scanning, RFID and mobile computing runs a software R&D center in Sri Lanka.

item.title: A Dutch founder searched the world for engineering talent and chose Sri Lanka. Meet Gapstars
item.description: Since 2015 Gapstars has built dedicated engineering teams in Colombo for 75+ European and international companies.

item.title: A company picked in the UK Ministry of Defence's search for future tech leaders builds its training software in Colombo. Meet SimCentric
item.description: SimCentric's simulation and virtual reality software helps armed forces train safely. Its engineering centre has been in Sri Lanka since day one.

item.title: A Colombo company is helping build Estonia's national AI infrastructure. Meet Rootcode
item.description: Rootcode works on platforms for the world's most digital government and ranked first in Asia Pacific at the 2025 APICTA Awards.

item.title: 600 Sri Lankan finance professionals run the books for clients in 10+ countries. Meet Infomate
item.description: A John Keells Holdings subsidiary turned Sri Lanka's depth in accounting talent into a global shared services business.

item.title: JPMorganChase acquired a wealth platform founded by two Sri Lankans. Meet WealthOS
item.description: First client in 2023, acquired in January 2026. The 50+ engineer team in Sri Lanka joined JP Morgan Personal Investing.

item.title: Sri Lanka made the biggest jump in Startup Genome's 2026 emerging ecosystem rankings
item.description: The Global Startup Ecosystem Report 2026 ranks Sri Lanka third in Asia for affordable tech talent after a climb of more than 65 positions.

item.title: One founder's bet on a purpose built IT park now houses 85+ companies and 8,000 professionals. Meet Orion City
item.description: In 2007 Sri Lanka had no purpose built IT park. Jeevan Gnanam started one with 10,000 sq. ft. and Virtusa as the first tenant.

item.title: An Australian founder built a 200 person tech team in Colombo in two years. Meet Dijital Team
item.description: Founded in 2023, ranked the 4th Best Workplace in Sri Lanka in its size category by 2025.

item.title: The Colombo company behind a travel platform with a billion bookings also built an electric supercar. Meet CodeGen
item.description: CodeGen's travelbox platform serves 250+ travel businesses. The same company built Vega and Sri Lanka's largest EV charging network.

item.title: Sri Lankan engineers are writing software for European vehicle programs. Meet Inivos
item.description: Founded in 2019, Inivos has grown to 180+ professionals and partnered with ICT Automotive to work on embedded and electric vehicle software.

item.title: A self taught founder won a billionaire's backing, delivered, then bought his company back. Meet Surge Global
item.description: Bhanuka Harischandra founded Surge in Colombo in 2015. It now has 400+ people and a contract with the government of Qatar.

item.title: A Stanford graduate built a $15M business placing Sri Lankan talent with US startups. Meet Oceans
item.description: Ian Myers worked remotely with a Sri Lankan team for two years, then built a company around what he saw.

item.title: EY runs its global delivery network from nine countries. Sri Lanka is one of them
item.description: EY Global Delivery Services employs 90,000+ people worldwide. Its Sri Lanka centre has grown to 500+ staff.

item.title: It started with 10 engineers in a Colombo home, listed on Nasdaq and sold for $2 billion. Meet Virtusa
item.description: Kris Canekeratne cofounded Virtusa in 1996 and led it for 25 years. Colombo remains one of its most important technology centres.

item.title: A global business process leader has delivered from Colombo for 20 years. Meet WNS Sri Lanka
item.description: WNS has operated in Sri Lanka since 2004 and employs 800+ people across two facilities in Colombo.

item.title: The world's largest foodservice company builds its core software in Colombo. Meet Sysco LABS
item.description: Sysco LABS Sri Lanka works on the same codebase and sprint cycles as Sysco's teams in Texas.

item.title: A software company built in Colombo sold for $600 million. Meet WSO2
item.description: EQT acquired WSO2 in 2024. 80% of its 780 engineers are Sri Lankan, and its headquarters is still Colombo.

item.title: Why IFS, HCLTech, EY and Sysco keep building in Sri Lanka
item.description: These are scaled operations, some of them decades old. Four reasons come up every time.

item.title: The universities behind Sri Lanka's engineering pipeline
item.description: Moratuwa has been a top contributor to Google Summer of Code since 2004. SLIIT serves 25,000+ students.

item.title: Sri Lanka's IT and BPM exports hit $1.645 billion in 2025
item.description: 500+ tech companies and 120,000+ IT professionals make ICT one of the country's largest export earners.

item.title: The London Stock Exchange picked a Colombo company for its trading platform, then bought the company. Meet MillenniumIT
item.description: The Millennium Exchange platform processes trades in 125 microseconds and powers exchanges on several continents.
